macro_markets.query: What are the most important macroeconomic and stock market news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major index movements, Fed/central bank news, and significant company earnings or announcements.

items.title: U.S. stocks suffer sharp selloff as AI concerns intensify
items.summary: The S&P 500 fell 3.59% to 6,918.45, the Nasdaq Composite dropped 5.13% to 22,654.15, and the Dow declined 1.85% to 48,188.18. The selloff followed a weak reaction to Anthropic’s market debut and renewed concerns about excessive AI valuations.[1]

items.title: S&P 500 and Dow enter correction territory
items.summary: The S&P 500 and Dow confirmed corrections after a steep weekly decline, while the Nasdaq recorded its worst weekly performance in six years. Technology shares led losses as investors reassessed the sustainability of AI-related spending and valuations.[1][5]

items.title: Fed officials signal support for another rate hike
items.summary: Fed Governor Lisa Cook and Philadelphia Fed President Anna Paulson argued that interest rates may not yet be high enough to contain inflation. Markets reportedly assigned a high probability to a December increase, with upcoming PCE inflation data expected to influence the outlook.[1]

items.title: AI infrastructure spending weighs on major technology companies
items.summary: Alphabet, Meta, and Amazon reportedly posted negative third-quarter free cash flow as capital spending on AI infrastructure surged. The spending pressure added to investor concerns about whether AI-related investments will generate adequate returns.[5]

items.title: Nvidia earnings remain a major market focus
items.summary: Nvidia reported third-quarter revenue of $115.8 billion, up 103% year over year, and forecast fourth-quarter sales of $130 billion. The company guided gross margin to 71%–72%, keeping its results central to the broader debate over AI demand and valuations.[8]

items.title: Asian markets extend losses after Wall Street rout
items.summary: Asian equities continued to decline following the U.S. selloff, while U.S. stock-index futures rebounded in early trading. The market remained focused on AI-sector volatility and expectations for tighter Federal Reserve policy.[9]

crypto_news.query: What are the most significant cryptocurrency and blockchain news from the past 24 hours? Include major price movements, regulatory news, and notable project developments.

items.title: Bitcoin and Ethereum rebound; broader crypto market turns higher
items.summary: Bitcoin rose about 1.8% over 24 hours to roughly $61,271 after trading as low as $58,769, while Ethereum gained about 2.3% to approximately $1,724.33. Solana traded above $70 and NEAR rose about 7.4% after a governance proposal reduced its inflation rate to 1.6%.

items.title: SEC charges eight Colorado entities over alleged $37 million crypto fraud
items.summary: The U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission charged eight entities registered in Colorado, alleging that they used false information and misleading promises through fake investment advisers and crypto trading platforms to defraud U.S. investors of more than $37 million.

items.title: Hong Kong proposes broader virtual-asset licensing rules
items.summary: Hong Kong published legislation that would extend mandatory licensing or registration to virtual-asset dealing, advisory, management and custody services, expanding oversight beyond trading platforms.

items.title: Institutional investor reportedly buys more than $1 billion in Bitcoin
items.summary: Abraxas Capital reportedly withdrew 17,597 Bitcoin from Binance and Kraken at an average price of about $59,206, representing roughly $1.04 billion in purchases as Bitcoin traded below $60,000.

items.title: GENIUS Act will restrict stablecoin interest payments in 2027
items.summary: Under the reported implementation timetable, payment stablecoin issuers will be prohibited from paying interest or yield solely because users hold, use or retain stablecoins beginning January 18, 2027.

items.title: Chainflip reports approximately $12 million asset theft
items.summary: Chainflip reportedly suffered a theft involving about $12 million in assets and offered a 10% white-hat bounty for the return of funds.

items.title: Hyperliquid weekly revenue rises to $21.22 million
items.summary: Hyperliquid generated approximately $21.22 million in revenue over the past seven days, up 15.51% from the previous week, with perpetual contracts accounting for about 97% of revenue.

items.title: Wrapped Monero token XMR1 crashes 99% after large transfer
items.summary: XMR1, a Monero-wrapped token on Hyperliquid, reportedly plunged 99% after 5.2 million tokens moved from the creator’s wallet to a newly created address, while about $13.2 million flowed to Ethereum.

ai_news.query: What are the most important artificial intelligence and machine learning news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include new model releases, company announcements, research breakthroughs, and industry trends.

items.title: Google releases Gemini 4 Neon
items.summary: Google introduced Gemini 4 Neon, a lower-cost frontier model with a reported 1-million-token context window and emphasis on coding, analysis, and enterprise workflows.[1][2]

items.title: OpenAI launches GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol
items.summary: OpenAI reportedly released GPT-6.2 Astra for demanding professional work and GPT-6.2 Sol as a cheaper everyday model, with both offering 1-million-token context windows.[2][8]

items.title: Anthropic-linked AI proof of the Riemann Hypothesis reported
items.summary: Anthropic mathematician Levent Alpöge reportedly announced a proof developed with Claude and formalized in Lean; external mathematicians were still reviewing the result, so it remains an unconfirmed research claim.[1][10]

items.title: Alibaba releases Qwen4-Max
items.summary: Alibaba reportedly released Qwen4-Max, a 2.4-trillion-parameter mixture-of-experts model with a 1-million-token context window and 71 billion active parameters per token.[3][10]

items.title: Thinking Machines Lab releases Inkling 2 Mini
items.summary: Thinking Machines Lab released Inkling 2 Mini, an open-weight 26.4-billion-parameter looped-transformer mixture-of-experts model with 3.4 billion active parameters per token, designed to run on a laptop.[7][8]

items.title: Microsoft announces new MAI model family
items.summary: Microsoft reportedly announced seven models spanning coding, cybersecurity, image generation, speech, transcription, and decision-making at Ignite 2026.[4]

items.title: AI infrastructure costs rise amid hardware shortages
items.summary: Dell, HPE, Lenovo, and Supermicro reportedly sought AI-server contract price increases of up to 45%, citing shortages of memory and printed-circuit boards.[3]

items.title: AI stocks face reported $1.7 trillion selloff
items.summary: AI-related equities reportedly suffered a roughly $1.7 trillion market-value decline, highlighting growing concern about AI valuations despite continued model and agent releases.[1]

gaming.query: What are the most notable video game and gaming industry news from the past 24 hours? Include game releases, announcements, esports, and industry developments.

items.title: Unreal Engine 6 to drop Blueprints scripting system
items.summary: Epic Games has announced that Unreal Engine 6, including its early-access release, will not include the long-standing Blueprints visual-scripting system or the Actor Gameplay Framework. The change is being positioned alongside a greater emphasis on AI-assisted coding.[1]

items.title: Supercell recruits creator of Clash Royale AI cheat
items.summary: Supercell has reportedly brought in the creator of a sophisticated Clash Royale cheating tool to help develop anti-cheat technology. The company has not yet announced specific bans or implementation dates.[2]

items.title: Dota 2 receives major 7.42 update
items.summary: Valve released Dota 2 patch 7.42, changing hero health and Strength scaling, relocating the Twin Gates, and moving the Tormentor spawn time to 15 minutes.[3]

items.title: The Wolf Among Us Remastered listed for Switch
items.summary: Nintendo’s eShop reportedly lists The Wolf Among Us Remastered for Nintendo Switch on November 29, following delays that pushed the Switch version behind releases on other platforms.[3]

items.title: Art the Clown coming to Dead by Daylight
items.summary: Art the Clown from the Terrifier film series is set to join Dead by Daylight as a new killer on November 24, with the character expected to be formally revealed at The Horror Game Awards.[8]

items.title: Xbox announces 20 games for the week
items.summary: Microsoft has published a schedule listing 20 games coming to the Xbox ecosystem from November 23 through 27, including titles launching through the Microsoft Store.[9]

items.title: The Finals Grand Major set for Stockholm
items.summary: The Finals Grand Major 2026 is scheduled to begin November 27 in Stockholm, with Twitch drops, spectator rewards, and prediction contests planned around the tournament.[4]

items.title: Jam City cuts approximately 60 jobs
items.summary: Jam City has reportedly laid off around 60 employees, or about 10% of the workforce associated with Harry Potter: Hogwarts Mystery. No game closures were reported.[5]
